World Economic Outlook – July
   2026 Update



          Introduction

        Key Highlights of WEO – July 2026 Update

        Uneven Momentum Continues amid Opposing Shocks

      Introduction

                                                  The World Economic Outlook (WEO) is the
                                                             flagship publication of the International
                                                   Monetary Fund (IMF) that provides a
         Overview                                    comprehensive assessment of the global
                                                  economy, including growth prospects, inflation
                                                                trends, risks, and policy challenges across the
                                                          IMF's 190 member countries.

                                                  The WEO serves as a key reference for
                                                         policymakers, financial institutions, investors,
         Purpose                                        researchers, and academics to monitor global
                                                   macroeconomic trends, assess systemic risks,
                                                   and formulate economic policies.

                                                  The full WEO Report is published twice a year,
           Publication Frequency
                                                              generally in April and October.

                                                  The IMF also releases World Economic Outlook
                                                    Updates in January and July to revise forecasts
           Interim Updates
                                                                        in response to rapidly changing global economic
                                                        developments.

                                                  The report provides short-term and medium-
                                                     term projections for major macroeconomic
                                                                   indicators, including Gross Domestic Product
         Key Economic Indicators Covered
                                                    (GDP) growth, consumer price inflation,
                                                   unemployment, fiscal balances, current account
                                                         balances, and global trade volumes.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 1

The WEO is one of the world's most authoritative
                                                              reports on the global economy, offering
          Significance                                  evidence-based forecasts, policy analysis,
                                                               regional outlooks, and assessments of emerging
                                                               global economic risks

     Key Highlights of WEO – July 2026 Update

                                                            Global economic growth is projected at 3.0% in
                                               2026 and 3.4% in 2027, lower than the 3.5%
          Global Economic Outlook                      average during 2024–25 and broadly unchanged
                                                       from the April 2026 World Economic Outlook
                                               (WEO) on a cumulative basis.

                                                  The moderate slowdown reflects the negative
                                                      impact of the Middle East war, partly offset by
         Key Drivers of Growth                            the technology-driven global upturn, fueled by
                                                               rapid advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and
                                                                                   its widespread adoption.

                                                  The economic impact varies depending on
         Uneven Impact Across Countries                  countries' exposure to the conflict and their
                                                                position in the global technology value chain.

                                                        Energy-exporting countries outside the conflict
                                                    zone benefit from improved terms of trade, while
         Winners from Current Trends                  economies integrated into the AI-driven
                                                       technology cycle experience stronger growth
                                                     even if they are net energy importers.

                                                        Energy-importing economies with limited
                                                                  participation in the technology value chain—
          Countries Facing Challenges
                                                               including many low-income countries—are
                                                       expected to witness weaker economic activity.

                                                            Global headline inflation is projected to increase
                                                       from 4.1% in 2025 to 4.7% in 2026, before
                                                          easing to 3.9% in 2027. The upward revision
          Global Inflation Outlook
                                                                indicates that the global disinflation trend,
                                                   underway since early 2024, has temporarily
                                                                       stalled.

         Downside Risks                             Key downside risks include: escalation of the
                                                      Middle East conflict, prolonged commodity price
                                                                         volatility, supply chain disruptions, tighter
                                                            global financial conditions, trade fragmentation,
                                                      a possible correction in technology-driven





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 2

market optimism, and limited policy buffers in
                                               many economies.

                                                                  Potential positive developments include faster
                                                          normalization of energy markets, stronger AI
                                                 and technology investments, renewed
         Upside Risks
                                                               international cooperation reducing trade
                                                                    barriers, and structural reforms that enhance
                                                    medium-term growth prospects.

                                                         Policymakers should prioritize restoring price
                                                                     stability through credible monetary policy, clear
         Monetary Policy Priorities                         central bank communication, central bank
                                                      independence, and strong financial sector
                                                            supervision.

                                                    Governments should rebuild fiscal buffers while
                                                             providing only temporary and targeted fiscal
           Fiscal Policy Priorities
                                                       support that protects vulnerable groups without
                                                                   distorting market price signals.

                                                                 Structural reforms should focus on strengthening
                                                     energy security, enhancing AI readiness,
           Structural Reform Priorities                     promoting domestic economic rebalancing, and
                                                          improving international cooperation to mitigate
                                                                  geopolitical and economic tensions.

     Uneven Momentum Continues amid Opposing Shocks

                                                  The global economy is being shaped by two
                                                     opposing forces: (i) the negative supply shock
                                                    from the Middle East war, and (ii) the positive
                                                       technology shock driven by rapid advances and
         Overview
                                                          adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Their
                                                        impact differs significantly across countries
                                                      depending on energy dependence and integration
                                                                     into the technology value chain.

                                                  The global economy has so far proved more
                                                                     resilient than expected. Although the war has
                                                              affected commodity prices, inflation
           Resilience of the Global Economy                 expectations, and financial conditions, the
                                                                   overall impact has been moderated by temporary
                                                                factors such as inventory drawdowns and
                                                          continued technological expansion.

        Commodity Price Developments               Commodity prices remain elevated but have
                                                     moderated following ceasefires and the Iran–US





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 3

Memorandum of Understanding. Energy prices
                                                        remain about 25% above pre-war levels, while
                                                            the oil futures curve remains in backwardation,
                                                                   reflecting continued supply disruptions and
                                                                  geopolitical risks.

                                                  The average petroleum spot price for 2026 is
                                                            projected at US$78 per barrel, lower than the
                                             US$82 projected in the April 2026 WEO
                                                           reference scenario and well below the US$100
            Oil Market Outlook
                                                 assumed under the adverse scenario. Temporary
                                                             inventory drawdowns have reduced the
                                                       immediate impact of supply disruptions through
                                                            the Strait of Hormuz.

                                                  The impact of higher energy prices differs across
                                                             countries due to differences in oil quality,
                                                         distance from suppliers, long-term supply
                                                      agreements, sanctions, taxes, subsidies, and
         Uneven Energy Price Impact
                                                     market regulations. Since the war began, retail
                                                          gasoline prices have risen by about 30% in
                                                    Emerging Asia compared with 15% in Latin
                                                       America.

                                                              Natural gas markets remain more regionally
                                                         fragmented. Since the conflict began, Liquefied
                                                           Natural Gas (LNG) prices have increased by
          Natural Gas Market
                                                      around 50% in Asia, 25% in Europe, and only
                                           10% in the United States (Henry Hub
                                                     benchmark).

                                                               Rising energy prices have pushed global
                                                         headline inflation higher for the third
                                                       consecutive month, interrupting the global
            Inflation Trends
                                                                      disinflation trend that began in early 2024. Core
                                                                      inflation, however, has remained relatively stable
                                                                        in most countries.

                                                                       Inflation expectations for 2026 have increased
                                                                 globally due to higher energy costs, while
                                                            expectations for 2027 remain relatively well
            Inflation Expectations
                                                         anchored. Countries with greater economic slack
                                                              or without fuel price controls have experienced
                                                                  larger increases in inflation expectations.

          Global Financial Conditions                       Global financial conditions have eased from their
                                                                 April 2026 peaks and remain relatively
                                                    accommodative despite periodic volatility.
                                                       Markets now expect higher policy interest rates,





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 4

contributing to rising long-term sovereign bond
                                                              yields across many countries.

                                                            Global GDP growth in the first quarter of 2026
                                                      reached 3.0% (quarter-on-quarter annualised),
          Global Growth Performance                      outperforming the 2.7% forecast in the April
                                               2026 WEO, although slowing from 3.8% in the
                                                                           final quarter of 2025.

                                                          Stronger-than-expected growth has been
                                                        supported by increasing use of renewable
                                                         energy, declining energy intensity of economies,
          Factors Supporting Growth
                                                                   fiscal support, and resilient domestic demand,
                                                     making many countries less vulnerable to rising
                                                       energy prices.

                                                  The positive growth surprise has been
                                                         concentrated in economies deeply integrated into
                                                            the global AI and semiconductor value chain.
                                                  The top four net exporters of AI-related
          Role of AI and Technology                    hardware—Taiwan Province of China, Republic
                                                            of Korea, Thailand, and Malaysia—recorded an
                                                       average positive growth surprise of 4.4
                                                      percentage points, while the rest of the world
                                                        recorded a slight negative surprise.

                                                         Republic of Korea: GDP grew 7.5%, driven by
                                                   booming semiconductor and AI hardware
                                                        exports despite heavy dependence on Middle
                                                            East energy imports.
                                                         China: Growth reached 8.1%, supported by
                                                            public infrastructure investment, high-tech
                                                        manufacturing, and exports, although domestic
                                                      consumption remained weak.
         Country Highlights                            Japan: GDP expanded 1.8%, led by exports, net
                                                               trade, and improving private consumption.
                                                  Germany: GDP grew 1.4%, double the April
                                                                 forecast, mainly due to stronger net exports.
                                                        United States: GDP increased 2.1%, slightly
                                                     below expectations but supported by business
                                                         investment, government spending, and
                                                                   intellectual property investment, despite weaker
                                                   consumer spending and higher imports.


           Overall Outlook                            The global economic outlook varies significantly
                                                      depending on countries' exposure to the Middle
                                                         East war and their integration into the global AI
                                                 and technology value chain. Economies





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 5

benefiting from technology exports or energy
                                                           exports are expected to outperform, while
                                                           energy-importing economies with limited
                                                              technological capabilities face slower growth.

                                                   IMF projections assume the Strait of Hormuz
                                                         begins reopening in mid-July 2026, with
                                                             conditions largely normalizing by March 2027.
          Baseline Assumptions
                                                     Temporary shortages are expected in some
                                                    emerging market and developing economies
                                                  (EMDEs) lacking strategic energy reserves.

                                                 Compared with 2025, crude oil prices are
                                                            projected to increase by 32%, natural gas prices
                                                    by 22%, fertilizer prices by 26%, and food
        Commodity Price Outlook                        prices by 8% in 2026. Average oil prices are
                                                            projected at US$89 per barrel, while Dutch TTF
                                                                 natural gas prices are expected to average
                                                     US$15.

                                                              Central banks are expected to maintain a less
                                                  accommodative monetary stance due to
                                                                persistent inflationary pressures. Fiscal policy is
         Monetary & Fiscal Policy Outlook                 projected to remain broadly neutral in advanced
                                                    economies during 2026 before tightening later,
                                                             while EMDEs are expected to gradually tighten
                                                                       fiscal policy throughout the forecast period.

                                                                 Existing trade policies and tariff structures are
                                                 assumed to remain unchanged through 2027.
                                                                 Geopolitical uncertainty is expected to stay
         Trade & Geopolitical Assumptions
                                                               elevated, while the current AI-driven technology
                                                          cycle is assumed to gradually moderate without
                                                           generating an additional productivity boom.

                                                            Global GDP growth is projected at 3.0% in 2026
                                                           before improving to 3.4% in 2027. Although
                                                           broadly unchanged from the April 2026 WEO,
          Global Growth Outlook
                                                               country-level outcomes differ considerably
                                                      depending on exposure to energy markets and
                                                           technology-driven growth.

                                                      World trade growth is projected to slow from
                                              5.0% in 2025 to 3.5% in 2026, before recovering
                                                                  to 4.3% in 2027. The slowdown reflects the
          Global Trade Outlook                           impact of tariffs, earlier front-loading of trade,
                                                   and the gradual reconfiguration of global supply
                                                           chains through trade diversion, rerouting, and
                                                       expanding technology-related trade.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 6

Growth in advanced economies is projected at
                                                   1.7% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027. Energy exporters
         Advanced Economies                              benefit from improved terms of trade, while
                                                       energy importers face greater challenges unless
                                                        supported by strong technology-related activity.

                                                  The US economy is projected to grow by 2.3% in
                                               2026 and 2.2% in 2027, supported by
                                                       technology investment, strong productivity,
          United States
                                                                   fiscal support, and its position as a net energy
                                                             exporter, limiting the impact of the Middle East
                                                                       conflict.

                                                     Growth is projected at 0.9% in 2026 and 1.2% in
                                                      2027, reflecting weaker consumer confidence,
          Euro Area                                        higher energy prices, and negative carry-over
                                                                 effects from the first quarter despite some fiscal
                                                         support measures.

                                                        United Kingdom: Growth slows to 1.0% in 2026
                                                           before recovering to 1.3% in 2027 as energy
                                                       market pressures ease. Japan: Growth
          United Kingdom & Japan
                                                      moderates to 0.6% in 2026 before improving
                                                                        slightly to 0.7% in 2027, supported by fiscal
                                                    measures cushioning higher energy costs.

                                                         Republic of Korea: Growth rises to 2.6% (2026)
                                                   and 2.5% (2027) due to strong global demand for
                                                     semiconductors and AI-related products.
         Korea & Canada                             Canada: Growth slows to 1.1% in 2026 before
                                                          improving to 1.7% in 2027, supported by stronger
                                                                 private investment and favorable commodity
                                                                  prices.

                                                     Growth in EMDEs is projected to slow to 3.8% in
                                               2026 before recovering to 4.5% in 2027, with
         Emerging Market & Developing Economies
                                                      performance differing according to commodity
         (EMDEs)
                                                    dependence, technology integration, tourism,
                                                           remittances, and financial conditions.

                                                         China: Growth slows to 4.6% due to higher oil
                                                              prices and structural challenges. India: Remains
                                              among the fastest-growing major economies with
                                             6.4% growth, driven by robust private
          China, India & ASEAN
                                                    consumption and services. Malaysia (4.7%),
                                                         Thailand (1.9%), and Vietnam (7.5%) benefit
                                                       from expanding data centres, AI-related exports,
                                                   and the global technology cycle.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 7

Small Island Developing States are expected to
                                                          record weaker growth due to higher energy
          Small Island Developing States (SIDS)
                                                             costs, slower tourism, and reduced remittance
                                                              inflows.

                                                           Regional growth is projected to decline sharply to
                                               0.7% in 2026, before rebounding strongly to
                                               6.5% in 2027 as energy exports recover. Iraq,
                                                         Kuwait, and Qatar are expected to contract
          Middle East & Central Asia                        sharply in 2026 before registering double-digit
                                                       growth in 2027. Saudi Arabia is relatively less
                                                              affected due to diversified export routes, while
                                                                Iran experiences a smaller contraction than
                                                              previously anticipated.

                                                           Regional growth remains broadly stable at 4.3%
                                                                   in 2026, although oil-importing countries face
                                                                     rising food and energy prices. Nigeria benefits
         Sub-Saharan Africa                           from macroeconomic reforms and stronger terms
                                                              of trade but continues to struggle with inflation
                                                   and food insecurity. South Africa is expected to
                                                       improve gradually through structural reforms.

                                                     Growth is projected at 2.4% in 2026 and 2.7% in
                                                      2027. Brazil maintains relatively resilient growth,
           Latin America & Caribbean                        while Mexico experiences modest acceleration
                                                        supported by less restrictive domestic policies
                                                             despite continued uncertainty.

                                                     Growth remains subdued at around 2.0%. Russia
                                                               benefits from stronger commodity export
                                                          revenues, whereas energy-intensive economies
         Emerging & Developing Europe
                                                           continue to face challenges from higher energy
                                                                costs, partly offset by increased defence
                                                          spending.

                                                            Global headline inflation is projected to increase
                                                       from 4.1% (2025) to 4.7% (2026) before
                                                               declining to 3.9% (2027), mainly due to higher
          Global Inflation Outlook
                                                     energy and food prices. Inflation forecasts have
                                                   been revised upward compared with the April
                                               2026 WEO.

                                                     Core inflation is expected to decline gradually,
                                                          reaching target levels by mid-2027 in the United
                                                   Kingdom, end-2027 in Japan and the United
         Core Inflation Outlook
                                                              States, and 2028 in the Euro Area. China's
                                                                   inflation is expected to rise gradually from its
                                                                currently low levels.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 8

Compared with the April 2026 WEO, global risks
                                                            are more balanced but remain tilted to the
                                                      downside. The principal uncertainty arises from
           Overall Risk Assessment                           geopolitical tensions in the Middle East,
                                                          although stronger AI-driven growth and smoother
                                                       energy market normalization provide upside
                                                                     potential.

                                            A renewed escalation of the Middle East conflict
                                                         could significantly weaken global growth by
          Major Downside Risk: Middle East Conflict         raising commodity prices, prolonging supply
                                                         shortages, increasing exchange rate volatility,
                                                   and intensifying inflationary pressures.

                                                  The relatively moderate increase in oil prices has
                                                   been supported by inventory drawdowns.
                                                       However, inventories are approaching multi-year
         Energy Market Risks
                                                           lows, and prolonged disruptions or increased
                                                          hoarding could trigger sharp and nonlinear
                                                         increases in energy prices.

                                                                Persistent disruptions in energy and fertilizer
                                                     markets could substantially worsen global food
                                                               insecurity, particularly in South Asia and Sub-
         Food Security Risks
                                                    Saharan Africa, where smallholder farmers face
                                                            higher production costs and limited purchasing
                                                         power.

                                                           Countries with limited foreign exchange
                                                        reserves and restricted fiscal space face greater
                                                                   risks of balance of payments crises, widening
          Risks to Emerging & Developing Economies
                                                               external imbalances, and macroeconomic
                                                                          instability due to rising food and energy import
                                                                costs.

                                                         Higher inflation and rising living costs could
                                                            increase social unrest, political instability, and
           Social & Political Risks
                                                                 election-related tensions, especially in vulnerable
                                                    low-income economies.

                                                               Rising global risk aversion could trigger capital
                                                            outflows, asset price corrections, and tighter
           Financial Market Risks                            financing conditions in emerging markets,
                                                                    particularly those with weaker macroeconomic
                                                          fundamentals.

         Impact of Rising Defence Spending               Increased military expenditure may temporarily
                                                          support aggregate demand but diverts resources
                                                away from more productive investments. If





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                 9

geopolitical tensions escalate into broader
                                                             warfare, the resulting humanitarian and
                                                  economic losses would outweigh any short-term
                                                    economic benefits.

                                                Renewed trade tensions, higher tariffs, non-
                                                                            tariff barriers, and restrictions on critical
         Trade Fragmentation Risks                        intermediate goods could disrupt global supply
                                                            chains, reduce output, increase production costs,
                                                   and weaken global economic growth.

                                                       High public debt levels reduce governments'
                                                                           ability to respond to new shocks. Concerns over
                                                                   fiscal sustainability could increase sovereign
           Fiscal Vulnerabilities
                                                        borrowing costs, tighten financial conditions, and
                                                            create refinancing pressures, particularly in
                                                            highly indebted developing countries.

                                                                     Falling Official Development Assistance (ODA)
                                                         could make fiscal adjustment more difficult for
                                                      low-income countries, weakening investments in
          Declining Development Assistance
                                                              health, education, and social protection,
                                                                especially amid risks such as Ebola outbreaks
                                                   and extreme El Niño-related climate events.

                                                                          Political interference with independent central
                                                  banks could weaken policy credibility, unanchor
         Monetary Policy Risks                                 inflation expectations, and require higher interest
                                                             rates for longer, thereby slowing economic
                                                                          activity.

                                                                                              If rapid AI investment leads to widespread
                                                             adoption, productivity improvements, and
                                                                 efficiency gains, medium-term global growth
         Upside Potential from AI                         could exceed current projections. These gains
                                                     would be larger if supported by investments in
                                                         energy, digital infrastructure, critical inputs, and
                                                      workforce reskilling.

                                                    To fully benefit from the AI revolution, low-
                                                  income countries must bridge gaps in electricity
          Challenges for Low-Income Countries
                                                        access, digital infrastructure, and human capital
                                                      development.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                10

If expectations regarding AI-driven profitability
                                                        prove overly optimistic, technology investment
                                                         could decline sharply. This may trigger significant
         Technology Market Risks
                                                              corrections in technology stock markets,
                                                                    particularly in economies heavily dependent on
                                                                AI-related industries.

                                            A correction in AI-related asset prices could
                                                       reduce household wealth, weaken private
                                                      consumption, tighten global financial
         Macroeconomic Spillovers from AI Correction
                                                             conditions, create balance sheet pressures, and
                                                       slow economic activity beyond the technology
                                                                  sector.

                                                        Rapid AI adoption may also increase
                                                         cybersecurity threats, potentially disrupting
          Cybersecurity Risks                                financial systems, digital payment
                                                                infrastructure, and confidence in the broader
                                                                          digital economy.

                                                           Stronger international cooperation, durable
                                                  peace agreements, reduced trade barriers,
                                                          increased foreign direct investment (FDI), and
                                                      comprehensive structural reforms could
         Upside Risks from International Cooperation      strengthen global growth by restoring supply
                                                              chains, improving investment confidence, and
                                                          addressing long-term challenges such as
                                                  economic fragmentation, ageing populations,
                                                   and technological transformation.


                                                         Policymakers face a difficult balancing act
                                                   between containing inflation, supporting
                                                  economic growth, and protecting vulnerable
                                                     households amid the combined effects of the
           Overall Policy Challenge
                                                      Middle East war and the AI-driven technology
                                                 boom. Policy responses must remain credible,
                                                                     flexible, and country-specific, while
                                                            strengthening international cooperation.

                                                  The primary objective of monetary policy should
                                                        remain price stability. Policy decisions should
         Monetary Policy Priority                              reflect each country's inflation dynamics, demand
                                                                conditions, fiscal position, and financial
                                                                       vulnerabilities.

         Response to Temporary Inflation              Where inflationary pressures are expected to be
                                                     temporary and inflation expectations remain well
                                                         anchored, central banks should broadly maintain





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                11

constant real interest rates, even if this requires
                                                             increasing nominal policy rates.

                                                                      In economies experiencing strong AI-led
                                                       investment and demand, central banks may need
         Response to Strong AI-Driven Demand
                                                                  to tighten policy further to prevent economic
                                                        overheating and persistent inflation.

                                                           Countries with inflation already above target,
                                                    weaker policy credibility, stronger exchange-rate
         Response to Persistent Inflation                  pass-through, or rising second-round inflation
                                                                 effects may require higher interest rates for
                                                         longer to keep inflation expectations anchored.

                                                                                              If growth weakens significantly and inflationary
                                                          pressures subside, central banks may cautiously
         Scope for Monetary Easing
                                                     ease monetary policy, provided that long-term
                                                            price stability remains secure.

                                                            Clear communication is a key policy instrument.
                                                              Central banks should transparently explain how
         Importance of Central Bank Communication     new economic data influence policy decisions
                                                             while preserving legal and operational
                                                    independence from political interference.

                                                                   Flexible exchange rates should remain the
                                                          primary shock absorber. However, in periods of
                                                         severe market stress, temporary foreign
         Exchange Rate & Financial Stability             exchange interventions or targeted capital flow
                                                  measures may complement macroeconomic
                                                                policy under the IMF Integrated Policy
                                                    Framework.

                                                                 Financial regulators should intensify monitoring of
                                                       banks, non-bank financial institutions, and
          Strengthening Financial Sector Resilience        sovereign risks, while ensuring adequate capital,
                                                                       liquidity, and reserve buffers to withstand future
                                                                    financial shocks.

                                                    Governments should gradually withdraw energy-
                                                              related fiscal support as market conditions
                                                             normalize. Broad-based subsidies, price
           Fiscal Policy Principles
                                                               controls, and tax cuts should generally be
                                                        avoided because they are costly, distort market
                                                                 incentives, and are difficult to reverse.

                                                Where fiscal support is necessary, it should be
                                                        temporary, well-targeted, and focused on
          Targeted Fiscal Support
                                                          vulnerable households, while remaining
                                                              consistent with overall macroeconomic stability.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                12

Government assistance to businesses should be
                                                                    limited to viable, energy-intensive firms,
                                                                conditional upon improvements in energy
         Support for Firms
                                                                efficiency. Support measures should include
                                                             clear sunset clauses, transparent eligibility
                                                                        criteria, and identifiable financing sources.

                                                           Countries should strengthen systems for
                                                                 delivering targeted cash transfers, enabling
           Building Better Social Protection Systems         scarce fiscal resources to be used more
                                                                       efficiently during future crises while reducing
                                                                          political pressures for broad-based subsidies.

                                                           Countries benefiting from higher commodity
                                                           prices or the AI-driven technology boom should
                                                           avoid excessive public spending and instead save
         Managing Commodity & Technology Windfalls
                                                              or invest windfall gains within a credible medium-
                                                     term fiscal framework that maintains debt
                                                                      sustainability.

                                                    Governments should restore fiscal space through
                                                          stronger tax administration, durable revenue
                                                     measures, efficient public expenditure, and
          Rebuilding Fiscal Space                           greater investment in infrastructure, skills, and
                                                          targeted social protection. High-debt countries
                                                         should also actively manage refinancing and
                                                                   interest-rate risks.

                                                                 Structural reforms should promote business
                                                  dynamism, expand renewable energy, improve
                                                     energy efficiency, strengthen AI readiness,
           Structural Reform Priorities
                                                        develop digital infrastructure, enhance
                                                        workforce skills, and establish strong data
                                                    governance and cybersecurity frameworks.

                                                        Major economies should pursue domestic
                                                             reforms, including economic rebalancing in
                                                          China, credible fiscal consolidation in the United
          Addressing Domestic Imbalances
                                                              States, and deeper Single Market integration in
                                                         the European Union, to strengthen global
                                                    economic stability.

                                                                   International trade rules should become more
                                                            transparent, predictable, and better aligned with
                                                 modern economic realities, including the growing
          Modernising Global Trade Rules
                                                        importance of services trade, digital trade, and
                                                      supply chain resilience. Regional trade
                                                      agreements should minimise market distortions.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                13

Greater international cooperation is needed to
                                                manage commodity market volatility, refugee
          Strengthening International Cooperation          flows, and global debt vulnerabilities. Countries
                                                         should avoid export bans, which worsen supply
                                                         shortages and increase global price volatility.

                                                  The IMF should continue providing liquidity
                                                          support where needed, while countries facing
                                                        debt distress should pursue timely debt
          Role of the IMF & Global Debt Frameworks
                                                                restructuring through mechanisms such as the
                                            G20 Common Framework and the Global
                                                       Sovereign Debt Roundtable.





World Economic Outlook – July 2026 Update                                                                                                14
